title: Really well executed app
body:
Really nicely done app. The way you can schedule events with natural language is nice, the various notification and delay options are great, and it feels like the developer really cared about creating a great experience. 

For years I’ve used my calendar as a todo list for important things, adding events when I think I might tackle it, but it’s a pain to keep on top of and if you miss an event you have to remember to manually reschedule. This app is basically the structure version of that workflow - items have times (super easy to enter), it reminds you at the time and also makes it trivial to defer by whatever time unit you like. 

My one very slight nit is I would love an option to use the standard iOS system font. The one it uses is fine and easy to read, I just like things to look consistent in general. But that’s a minor issue with an otherwise great app. Nice work.

title: Should be called “Nag” not “Due”
body:
I’ve used this app for at least 2 years now, and belatedly just realised I don’t just dislike this app, I despise it with every fibre of my being, so much so I have realised it is actually bad for my mental health. This app doesn’t remind you about stuff, it nags you and nags you and nags you until you want to scream! In the middle of a phone call? nag nag nag, obviously busy and not responding? nag nag nag. Pay “me attention” is its constant refrain, it like having a rude and badly behaved 4 yr old child in your pocket - permanently! I felt stressed every morning when my list of “nags” would start harassing me as soon as I woke up. If I had 2 nags go off at the same time I get double notifications simultaneously! Double nagging OMG! Even Apples restricted notifications don’t seem to be able to shut it up. I’ve actually thrown my phone at the wall because of its constant nagging.

There is literally nothing positive I can find to say about this app, even the “Undo edit reminder” is stupidly placed so that pressing the screen off button “undoes” your changes with the palm of your hand without realising it. 1 minute later you get nagged about the same thing all over again!

 I finally realised yesterday, this app doesn’t help me get stuff done, it just stresses me out about everything I’ve not got around to today, and loads up trepidation about tomorrow. I would willing burn every byte that belongs to this app, sadly I will just have to make do with “delete”.

I set a due time on say my phone, then change it on my iPad and that updated information doesn’t get updated on the other devices so someone else in the house or office will be complaining that the phone has been going off every few minutes even though the actual time was updated.

I even had one reminder that went off a day and a half early, I’m sure it was correctly set, its a bit odd. Slightly disappointing.

title: This is perfection
body:
Apple’s reminders in iOS 13 just got worse with the lack of days of the week on the scroll wheel - so I went looking for something that worked in an intuitive, logical user friendly manner - Due fulfilled that criteria and oh so much more!
I will not be able to fully do this app justice here, but to add a little weight to how grateful I am to the creators of this app, I can tell you this is the only review I ever written in my life... about anything.

The various ways in which one can enter the timings for the reminder is wonderful; partly because it is easy, fast, so ‘end user’ practical and highly customisable; allowing for different people’s preferences and yet clean, clear and simple. It also enabled me to import my existing reminders from the Apple Reminders app - which is very useful because some of my reminders are not so much time related - just when I get an idea for something I jot it down as a reminder so I can add a date and time if I need to later.
I think intuitive intelligence went into the making of this app.

I’m going to finish waffling by saying - if you need a wonderful one time purchase (which is important to me) reminders app then get this - it just works! And even if Apple are clever enough to add days of the week! into their reminders app... I won’t be going back to it. I wish I’d found this years ago.

And to the creators... thank you so very much.

title: Remind me to write a review about Due!
body:

I don’t add all my reminders to it, although that is an option too. Just the ones that are important one-offs plus some simple repeating tasks. 

The app now has the best subscription model available. Pay a small amount for a year and whatever new is added before your subscription runs out is to keep, even if you decide not to renew.  I am looking forward to some cool things being added to this app in the near future. New Shortcuts have just been added. Great.
 
I must also mention the Watch app. It’s so useful. Every time Due wants to remind me of something I get a tap on my wrist. Again, and again, and again. I can mark the task off, snooze it, or reschedule it. I can also set a task from my wrist if I feel like it.

title: iOS app great, WatchOS app useless

Pleased to report that the Watch companion app now behaves beautifully too. 

===

Previous review
—
The iOS app is great, I'd give it five stars, although the recent changes in iOS to the number of notifications have not been good for Due. Sometimes, "nag" reminders just stop. Otherwise great. 

The WatchOS app is a total waste of time, to the extent that I'd advise anyone buying with the intention of relying on the Watch app not to waste their money. Most of the time, the app is unresponsive, and completing reminders and stopping timers, when the app does work, is a lottery. It is one of those cases where you're better off using normal Watch notifications rather than this very poor Watch app. 1 star.

So, an average of three stars, then. I'll revisit this if the developer improves the WatchOS performance.

title: Nags me (in a good way)
body:
I have a problem with standard alarm apps; if I'm in the middle of something and they go off, I will dismiss them, finish what I was doing, then forget that the alarm had gone off. Yes, even if it only takes me a minute to finish what I was doing - because then something else will get my attention, then something else, and so on.

What's great about Due is that it gently nags me. It just politely goes "ping" then shuts up for a minute. Then it goes "ping" again, and I think "yeah, yeah, nearly done". Then it goes "ping" again, I finish up and there's my reminder on the lock screen. It doesn't buzz and jingle and beg for attention until I tell it to shut up, so I can ignore it until I'm ready.  And if I know I'm not going to be able to do the task for a while, it's blindingly quick to snooze it for a few minutes, hours or days.

I use this app dozens of times in a day. Very very useful.

title: Great, but a couple of crucial limitations
body:
This is a great app - I've just bought it for both iOS and Mac OS, and it synchronises and does everything it's supposed to. The crucial flaw as I see it at this stage is that the iOS version only synchronises (I'm using Dropbox as the sync method - I've no idea if it behaves the same using iCloud as the sync method) when you open and close the app. 

All the reminders work fine when the app isn't working - I get all the notifications and everything. But if I mark a reminder as complete on my Mac, that isn't synchronised with the iOS version until I open it. That's the crucial flaw. The whole purpose of a seamless reminders app (which this is in virtually every other respect) is that you don't have to put effort into doing it - it should do it for you. Devs, please please fix it so that it updates live in the background, so I never need to actually open the app on my iDevice except to create new reminders or mark old ones as done. If I have to remember to open it to make sure my reminders are up to date - what's the point?

The only other complaint I have is the default 'snooze' times in iOS - 1 minute or 1 hour is very limited compared to the broad range of times available in Mac OS. However, I know the devs are aware of this one and are working on it, so it's a 'for now' complaint only. 

Other than that, it's brilliant - I love the "do x tomorrow" and it'll mark it for 9am, or "do it in one hour" or "do it at 4". Lovely, very refreshing and simple and quick. The only other thing I would suggest is have voice-recognition - how much easier would it be to have all those features but just SAY to your iPhone "wake me up tomorrow at 6am" or something like that. Perhaps Apple will allow Siri integration in iOS 6… who knows?

Great app all in all - needs a bit more to make it all that it could be though.

Along with the repeat options of 1 minute and 1 hour, the following default options are required:

1. 5 mins
2. 10 mins
3. 20 mins
4. 30 mins
5. 45 mins

The other modification urgently required is more time allowed to quickly change the default snooze if needed.

I would like to see the automatic hiding function removed from the additional options for the reminder being modified.

There is no need to hide it automatically AND it's very annoying whilst modifying a current alarm to have it beeping away at you AND disappearing whist you are trying to get in with it.

This review is solely to spur the developer to fix these issues. This is otherwise a good program - it just needs some attention.

title: Due.App is a good "deadline" reminder App, But a poor "Nag" reminder App
body:
I would classify Due.App as an "Impending-reminder.App"  for imminent/urgent tasks   (Impending=about to happen). 

I have 2 needs for this type of App :- 

PURPOSE 1. Deadline reminder - time critical (continuous nag alarm every 1 minute)  
PURPOSE 2. Nag reminder (Nag alarms with a range of minute & hours options)

Due.App is a very good "deadline" reminder App, But a poor "Nag" reminder App.
I can set a reminder to nag every 1 minute or every 1 hour but nothing in between and so Due.App is too basic to be used as a "Nag" reminder app 

N.B Other Deadline reminder apps are nag.app  or EasyReminders.app
N.B. Other "NAG" reminder Apps (which meet the criteria above) are beep-me.app, nagger.app and alarmed.app (yoctoville -use the DayMinder feature and make sure preference>dayminder super user is switched on) 
 
If you make this preference:-
Settings > When adding reminders > Default snooze > None,  then you won't be tied to a global setting of 1 minute or 1 hour. You will be able to make the choice once they're created (click zzzz button)
